¹ This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri, during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel. ² When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, he said, "Go, take a promiscuous woman as your wife and have children with her, for this land has been utterly unfaithful to the LORD." ³ So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son. ⁴ The LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel, for soon I will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed at Jezreel, and I will bring the kingdom of Israel to an end. ⁵ In that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."

⁶ She conceived again and gave birth to a daughter. ¹¹ Then the people of Judah and the people of Israel will be reunited, and they will appoint one leader and will come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.

¹ Say to your brothers, "My People," and to your sisters, "Loved One." ² Confront your mother, confront her — for she is no longer my wife, and I am no longer her husband. I will make her like a desert, turn her into dry land, and let her die of thirst. ⁴ I will have no pity on her children, because they are the children of a prostitute. ⁵ Their mother has behaved shamefully. ⁶ So I will block her path with thornbushes and build a wall against her so she cannot find her way. ⁷ She will chase her lovers but not catch them; she will search for them but not find them. I will take away my wool and my linen that were meant to cover her nakedness. ¹⁰ Now I will expose her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers; no one will rescue her from my hand.

¹¹ I will put an end to all her celebrations — her annual feasts, her new moon festivals, her Sabbath days, all her appointed festivals. ¹² I will ruin her vines and fig trees, which she said were her wages from her lovers. She adorned herself with rings and jewelry and went after her lovers, but she forgot me, declares the LORD. ¹⁴ Therefore I am now going to lure her out into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her. ¹⁵ There I will give her back her vineyards, and will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will respond as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.

¹⁶ In that day, declares the LORD, you will call me "My Husband"; you will no longer call me "My Master." ¹⁷ I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips; no longer will their names be invoked. ¹⁸ In that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds in the sky, and the creatures that move along the ground. ²¹ In that day I will respond, declares the LORD — I will respond to the skies, and they will respond to the earth; ²² and the earth will respond to the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil, and they will respond to Jezreel. ²³ I will plant her for myself in the land; I will show my love to the one I called "Not Loved." ¹ The LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress — love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love the sacred raisin cakes." ² So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and about a homer and a lethek of barley. ³ Then I told her, "You are to live with me for many days; you must not be a prostitute or be intimate with any man, and I will behave the same way toward you." ⁴ For the Israelites will live for many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred stones, without ephod or household gods. ⁵ Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. ¹ Hear the word of the LORD, you Israelites, because the LORD has a charge to bring against you who live in the land: "There is no faithfulness, no love, no acknowledgment of God in the land. ² There is only cursing, lying, and murder, stealing and adultery; they break all bounds, and bloodshed follows bloodshed. ³ Because of this the land dries up, and all who live in it waste away; the beasts of the field, the birds in the sky, and the fish in the sea are swept away. ⁴ But let no one bring a charge or accuse another, for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest. ⁵ You stumble day and night, and the prophets stumble with you. So I will destroy your mother —

⁶ My people are destroyed from lack of knowledge. ¹¹ to prostitution; old wine and new wine take away their understanding. ¹² My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rod answers them; a spirit of prostitution leads them astray; they are unfaithful to their God. ¹³ They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, where the shade is pleasant. ¹⁶ The Israelites are stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. ¹¹ Ephraim is oppressed, trampled in judgment, intent on pursuing idols. ¹² I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the people of Judah. ¹³ When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah saw his sores, then Ephraim turned to Assyria, and sent to the great king for help. ¹¹ Also for you, Judah, a harvest is appointed. Whenever I restore the fortunes of my people,

¹⁶ They do not turn to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of their insolent words. For this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.

¹ Do not rejoice, Israel; do not be jubilant like the other nations. ¹¹ Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird — no birth, no pregnancy, no conception. ¹² Even if they bring up children, I will bereave them of every one. ¹⁶ Ephraim is blighted, their root is withered, they yield no fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay their cherished offspring. ¹⁷ My God will reject them because they have not obeyed him; they will be wanderers among the nations.

¹¹ Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh grain; so I will put a yoke on her fair neck. Because you have depended on your own strength and on your many warriors, ¹⁴ the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be devastated — as Shalman devastated Beth Arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to the ground with their children. ¹⁵ So will it happen to you, Bethel, because your wickedness is great. When that day dawns, the king of Israel will be completely destroyed.

To them I was like one who lifts a little child to the cheek, and I bent down to feed them. ⁵ Will they not return to Egypt and will not Assyria rule over them because they refuse to repent?

For I am God, and not a man — the Holy One among you. I will not come against their cities. ¹⁰ They will follow the LORD; he will roar like a lion. ¹¹ They will come from Egypt, trembling like sparrows, from Assyria, fluttering like doves. I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD. ¹² Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, Israel with deceit. And Judah is unruly against God, even against the faithful Holy One.

¹ Ephraim feeds on the wind; he pursues the east wind all day and multiplies lies and violence. He found him at Bethel and talked with him there — ⁵ the LORD God Almighty, the LORD is his name! ⁶ But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and wait for your God always.

¹ When Ephraim spoke, people trembled; he was exalted in Israel.
